mckinsey-soai-2025.title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
mckinsey-soai-2025.venue: McKinsey & Company (QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey), November 5, 2025
mckinsey-soai-2025.note: Byline lists Tara Balakrishnan as 'with'. Page now flags itself as older survey data and links to the 2026 edition.
mckinsey-soai-2025.figures: Online survey June 25 to July 29, 2025; 1,993 participants in 105 nations; 62% at least experimenting with AI agents (23% scaling plus 39% experimenting); 23% scaling an agentic AI system in at least one function; no more than 10% scaling agents in any given function.

mckinsey-soai-2026.title: The state of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
mckinsey-soai-2026.venue: McKinsey & Company (QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey), August 25, 2026
mckinsey-soai-2026.note: Newer edition that supersedes the 2025 page; not cited in the source paper, recorded for context.
mckinsey-soai-2026.figures: Online survey May 4 to June 8, 2026; 1,719 participants in 97 nations; about two in ten report reaching the scaling phase with AI agents across the organization.

sailpoint-agents-2025.title: SailPoint research highlights rapid AI agent adoption, driving urgent need for evolved security
sailpoint-agents-2025.venue: SailPoint press release, Austin, TX, May 28, 2025; report 'AI agents: The new attack surface' (survey by Dimensional Research)
sailpoint-agents-2025.note: Figures taken from the press release; underlying report PDF not opened. Fielding dates not stated.
sailpoint-agents-2025.figures: 353 qualified participants, IT professionals with enterprise security responsibilities across 5 continents; 82% of organizations already use AI agents; 44% have policies in place to secure them; 92% say governing AI agents is critical.
sailpoint-agents-2025.discrepancy: The page says 44% have policies 'to secure' AI agents, not policies 'governing' them.

ms-wti-2026.title: Agents, human agency, and the opportunity for every organization (2026 Work Trend Index Annual Report)
ms-wti-2026.venue: Microsoft WorkLab, May 5, 2026; survey by Edelman Data x Intelligence
ms-wti-2026.note: No individual byline. Fielding stated as Feb 18 to Apr 7, 2026 in methodology, Apr 20 in one figure note.
ms-wti-2026.figures: 20,000 AI-using knowledge workers in 10 markets (2,000 each); organizational factors account for more than 2x the reported AI impact of individual factors (67% vs 32%), via random forest permutation importance on 19,854 respondents; associational, not causal.
ms-wti-2026.discrepancy: The page reports about twice the permutation importance for self-reported AI impact (67% vs 32%), not twice the outcome variance, and labels it associational.

weill-woerner-2026.title: Leveraging Digital Colleagues for Enterprise Value
weill-woerner-2026.venue: MIT CISR Research Briefing No. XXVI-4, April 16, 2026
weill-woerner-2026.note: Digital colleagues defined as AI-enabled systems that collaborate with humans to perform complex work.
weill-woerner-2026.figures: MIT CISR 2025 Digital Colleagues Survey, N=132 organizations, fielded September (early fall) 2025; 75% of respondents predicted an average 25% increase in revenue per employee over three years.

nccoe-agent-idauth-2026.title: Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
nccoe-agent-idauth-2026.venue: NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence, draft concept paper (Initial Public Draft), February 5, 2026; comments closed April 2, 2026
nccoe-agent-idauth-2026.note: CSRC lists the title as '[Concept Paper] ... Software and Artificial Intelligence Agent ...'; PDF cover lists 'Bill Fisher'. PDF: https://www.nccoe.nist.gov/sites/default/files/2026-02/accelerating-the-adoption-of-software-and-ai-agent-identity-and-authorization-concept-paper.pdf. No DOI.
nccoe-agent-idauth-2026.figures: No quantitative figures; seeks feedback on applying identity and authorization standards to enterprise AI agent use cases.

authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI)
nist-ai-agent-standards-2026.title: AI Agent Standards Initiative
nist-ai-agent-standards-2026.venue: NIST initiative page; announced by CAISI on February 17, 2026; page last updated August 14, 2026
nist-ai-agent-standards-2026.figures: Three pillars: industry-led standards, community-led open protocols, research on agent security and identity; deliverables include a CAISI RFI on agent security and the NCCoE identity concept paper.

csa-atf-blog-2026.title: The Agentic Trust Framework: Zero Trust Governance for AI Agents
csa-atf-blog-2026.note: Author affiliation MassiveScale.AI. Blog states no specification version.
csa-atf-blog-2026.figures: Five core elements (identity, behavior, data governance, segmentation, incident response) and four maturity levels (Intern, Junior, Senior, Principal).

atf-spec-v091.title: Agentic Trust Framework Specification
atf-spec-v091.venue: Version 0.9.1, Public Review Draft, last updated April 2026; GitHub massivescale-ai/agentic-trust-framework; stewardship transferring to CSAI Foundation (CSA press release, April 29, 2026)
atf-spec-v091.note: Spec file carries no author or license line; repository page gives author Woodruff and CC BY 4.0. agentictrustframework.ai shows 'ATF v1'. Stewardship release: https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/press-releases/2026/04/29/csai-foundation-announces-key-milestones-to-secure-the-agentic-control-plane
atf-spec-v091.discrepancy: The v0.9.1 draft is hosted on the author's GitHub, not on cloudsecurityalliance.org, and the spec site labels it ATF v1.

anthropic-mcp-2024.title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol
anthropic-mcp-2024.note: No individual byline; page credits David Soria Parra and Justin Spahr-Summers as MCP creators.
anthropic-mcp-2024.figures: Announces open-sourcing of MCP as a standard for connecting AI assistants to data sources and tools.

authors: Model Context Protocol a Series of LF Projects, LLC
mcp-spec-2026-07-28.title: Model Context Protocol Specification, revision 2026-07-28
mcp-spec-2026-07-28.note: Versioning page states the current protocol version is 2026-07-28; lead maintainers David Soria Parra and Den Delimarsky (governance page).
mcp-spec-2026-07-28.figures: Current revision 2026-07-28; handshake-based revisions are 2025-11-25 and earlier.
mcp-spec-2026-07-28.discrepancy: The current specification is issued by the MCP project under LF Projects, LLC, not by Anthropic.

google-a2a-2025.title: Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
google-a2a-2025.figures: Announcement of the A2A open protocol for agent interoperability.

a2a-spec-v1.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
a2a-spec-v1.venue: a2a-protocol.org, Latest Released Version 1.0.0; project under the Linux Foundation-directed Agentic AI Foundation (blog, August 27, 2026)
a2a-spec-v1.note: Spec page has no date; the v1.0 release post is listed as March 12, 2026 on the blog index, but the post itself failed to open.
a2a-spec-v1.discrepancy: The current spec is v1.0.0 under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, not a Google-issued specification.
